page.overview:
Who is Elizabeth Gelman?

Dr. Elizabeth Gelman was the head of research at the San Diego Zoo and a friend of Dr. Ian Malcolm in .

Gelman was first mentioned in by Malcolm after he told his assistant Beverly told call her as he wanted Gelman to examine the contents of the strange animal Richard Levine sent him. She was head of research at the San Diego Zoo and examined gorillas, koala bears and a particular snow leopard named Dorje which bit Malcolm's hand after he attempt to pet it. She examined the content of the strange animal, first telling Malcolm her colleagues heard of the "unknown animals showing up in Costa Rica."

Under a light and slide projector she showed him that it was in a "state of very advanced necrosis" and that a close exanimation first indication that it was some kind of lizard. One cell showed it was a chameleon and male. The subcutaneous layers were surrounded by smooth muscle fibers, not characteristic of any lizard and the whole side indicated it was not one. There were chromatophores, or pigment-bearing cells, indicating it's skin could change color. Both her and Malcolm could not figure out what animal it was. However, she told him it was from a 'Site B' - Malcolm forgot to check the specimen which had a tag reading that. Gelman surmized that the tag was placed on the creature when it was young. She further noted it was exposed to some acid and Malcolm wondered if it was volcanic fumes. She further identified it as a radio tag and remarked somebody is rearing these strange animals and gets no answer from him. As he left, she gave him two last pieces of information: there was a foreign cell on the specimen, indicating the animal was in some fight. The section information was that "there were signs of chronic vasoconstriction in the arterial vessels," meaning it lived in a strainous environment. It was this information from the tag which led Malcolm to believe Levine was correct; that dinosaurs existed somewhere again.
